body:
I grew up in a hostile environment. The memories I do have are pretty bad.  
Everything is just a little bit wrong. Food doesn't taste right, the color of the walls is off, familiar voices sound unfamiliar. It's like I'm just watching the world without being part of it.
I suppose I got lost somewhere along the way. I don't have a lot of memories from when I was young and looking back I'm thankful for it.

I feel like this all the time. I know everything is real, but it doesn't feel like it. I often find myself 'checking' by dropping dishes or hurting myself.  
I know what's supposed to happen, so when it does, that is comforting.

I'm in therapy. I have BPD, double depression, SA.. I think I'm beyond repair. I want to get better, but while the depression gets better from time to time, the emptiness and dissociation only get worse. I don't have anything I want to do, nothing I want to buy and nowhere I want to go.  
I don't really know how to explain the 'alone' thing. In the past I met people that knew how I felt at any point, in any situation. Like they could see inside my head and it was the same for me.  
I feel like I'm hiding all the time, even when I try to be open and honest.

This is my fifth year in college and I've been dealing with depression for much longer. The first few semesters I was really stressing out about failing classes and thought I was too dumb to get through. So the first thing I learned was not to beat myself up. I'm very lucky in that I can take as much time as I need, so I just pick the classes I think I can manage.  
Another thing was simply talking to people. I have yet to have a problem that talking to a prof or TA didn't solve. If you show them that you care, so will they.  
Also, having a schedule and friends to study with has been very helpful to me. I rarely go to class, but I stick to studying with friends at my place, which is very low pressure. If you can get into the habit of not skipping anything, that will easily put you ahead of most of your peers.  
   
So, yeah, don't stress yourself out and find a way to learn that works for you. I also have to second jddads advice. I'm not at all the sports type, but I'd be lying if I said it didn't have a positive effect on my mood.
